Definition: Is the register integrated with the national ID system?
Comments: Digital ID/NIR is based on and connected to civil registration modules (Birth & Death; Marriage & Divorce), indicating partial-to-strong linkage between civil registration and national ID register.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: World Bank GovTech report (2021) states civil registration and the NID are administered by the same authority (NICR) with closely linked front-end processes and a shared back-end database; a single unique lifetime ID number is generated at registration and printed on the birth certificate, NID card, passport and death certificate. This indicates full rather than partial integration, so the score is revised from 4 to 5 (Fully integrated nationwide).

Definition: Does the government maintain a digital population register?
Comments: Lesotho’s National ID system (National Identity Register/NIR) is a digital database managed by NICR (Ministry of Home Affairs) and was launched in July 2013; the system has “close to universal coverage” with >85% of eligible population covered (>1.2m of 1.4m) and collects biometrics (ten fingerprints).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed by two World Bank sources: the National Identity Register, launched July 2013, is operated nationwide via 15 enrolment centres and 10 mobile registration units. Deployment status (5, Fully deployed nationwide) is distinct from eligible-population coverage (~85%), which is captured elsewhere. Score confirmed unchanged.
